inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement: no equity-settled share-based payment expense since FY2020 (FY2019 RMB0.3m, FY2018 RMB0.6m). Share option scheme exists but no options outstanding per H1 FY2026 interim; SBC-zero market, rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 and H1 FY2026 repurchases nil; FY2024 RMB78.8m (shares cancelled October 2024, count 2,778.6m -> 2,725.0m). Flat count is the actual state, not a convention the company has yet to pay for.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in CNY then converted at CNY/HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10). Parity check via the USD legs: USD/HKD 7.8472 / USD/CNY 6.6922 = 1.1726 vs the direct cross 1.1721, a 0.04% tie confirming rate and direction (1 CNY buys more than 1 HKD). No dual listing of the parent exists for a price parity check; the 67.6%-owned subsidiary TG Tech (920068.BJ) trades in RMB on the Beijing Stock Exchange but is not the same security. refresh_price.py moves the price and not this rate -- re-check the rate on any later refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX Friday close; valuation date is a Sunday)
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,725,000,000 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, basic EPS note); no dilutive instruments outstanding so diluted = basic. Held flat: SBC is zero and no non-SBC issuance is planned at parent level (TG Tech raised equity at the subsidiary, captured as NCI leakage, not as parent dilution).
inputs.net_debt_note: At 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim): bank loans RMB4,061.1m (current 99.5 secured + 1,509.7 unsecured + 1,083.7 current portion of non-current; non-current 206.6 secured + 2,245.3 unsecured less 1,083.7 reclassified) PLUS contingent redeemable capital contributions by third-party investors in TG Tools RMB360.3m (note 18 'Other financial liabilities'; down from RMB893.6m at FY2025 after RMB544.5m was redeemed in H1 FY2026, financed by new bank debt -- that redemption is why borrowings rose). Debt-like: it bears interest (RMB11.2m finance cost in H1) and repayments sit in financing. Total debt-like 4,421.4. Cash 1,324.6 plus time deposits 605.0 (not pledged) = 1,929.5; pledged deposits of 115.9 excluded as restricted. Net debt 2,491.9. Interest income on cash and time deposits (FY2025 RMB24.1m) is stripped from the FCF base because the deposits are added back here (matching-asset rule).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. China 10y CGB ~1.8%; China ERP ~6.5%; beta ~1.1 for a small-cap cyclical specialty-steel maker gives a cost of equity ~9%. Bank loans cost 2.2-4.8% pre-tax (~2.9% after a 15% HNTE rate) and debt is ~38% of market capital structure, so a mechanical WACC is ~6.5%. House rate set at 9.0%: an HK-listed, PRC-domiciled small-cap industrial with a 51%-controlling family shareholder, a separately listed subsidiary, rising leverage and chronically weak cash conversion carries a size/governance/liquidity premium that a mechanical CAPM on a thinly traded stock does not capture. The 9% is the same rate used in the bull and bear scenarios: cyclicality and customer concentration are charged in the flows (scenario paths and weights), not again in the discount rate. Charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. No lease liabilities on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet; right-of-use assets are prepaid PRC land-use rights (amortisation RMB3.2m per half, inside D&A). Reported OCF is therefore not flattered by IFRS 16 reclassification.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Consolidated flows include 100% of 67.6%-owned TG Tech (titanium alloy, BSE-listed May 2025) and the TG Tools minorities; the NCI share of profit was 11.8% (FY2023), 10.3% (FY2024), 8.6% (FY2025) and 2.5% (H1 FY2026, titanium trough). An ~8% leakage of post-tax profit (~7pp of EBIT) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path on top of the cash tax rate; the bull path carries more leakage because titanium is where the bull growth sits. No NCI deduction in the bridge (book NCI RMB528.4m at 30 June 2026 is NOT deducted, and TG Tech's BSE market value is not deducted either -- deducting a market value for a sub whose flows are DCF-valued here would be inconsistent). Calibration: FY2025 EBIT 587.7 x (1 - 0.15) = 499.5 vs attributable NI 400.2 + after-tax net finance costs ~127 = ~527; ties within non-operating noise (FX gains, other income).
inputs.cash_tax_note: PRC subsidiaries enjoy the 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate plus R&D super-deductions; Thailand plant at 0% to May 2027 then 20%. P&L effective rate FY2025 6.7%, FY2024 2.0%, FY2023 9.8%; cash taxes paid FY2025 were a net RMB26.7m refund. The cash-tax component of the combined driver starts at 8% and ramps to 13% by year 10 (the HNTE status is re-certified every three years and is not a given in perpetuity).
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer with receivables 4,041 + inventories 2,810 - payables 1,631 = ~RMB5.2bn net working capital on RMB4.9bn TTM revenue (over 100%). Growth consumes cash: wc_capture is -45% of the revenue change in base. FY2018-25 cumulative owner FCF was only ~RMB715m (avg ~RMB90m/yr, ~2% of revenue) against ~RMB3.5bn of cumulative attributable profit because receivables (incl. bills) and inventories grew ~RMB2.5bn+ on flat revenue -- stretched terms to European customers and bills-receivable financing of domestic buyers. The component build assumes that stock stops growing faster than revenue (H1 FY2026 OCF RMB440m shows it can release); if terms keep lengthening the bear case is the right one. The modelled mid-cycle owner-FCF margin (~8-9%) is well above the realised 8-year average, and this is the single assumption most worth challenging.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted -- routed via dcf-methods as a non-US cyclical operating company (specialty steel, cutting tools, titanium alloy), with the adaptations file applied: CNY-built WACC, CNY->HKD quote bridge, no leases, NCI as leakage in the flows, interest income stripped against time deposits in the bridge, SBC-zero. Mid-cycle normalisation: base EBITDA margin 20.5% in FY2026 (H1 gross margin 24.8% vs 18.9%) fading to 19.8%, against a FY2020-25 average of 19.8% and FY2018-19 of 12.5-15.5%. Revenue has been flat for eight years (FY2018 5,022 -> FY2025 4,719); base growth of 5% in FY2026 (H1 +5.5%, June HSS price rises, titanium recovery) fading to 2.5% is a modest premium to history. Terminal cap 12x for a cyclical. Reported FCF in the CSV is unlevered: interest paid (FY2025 RMB160.8m) is classified in financing. House and street coincide (SBC zero), so band_position is null. FY0 = FY2025 (31 Dec year end); valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026 with H1 reported.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: equity 5yr CAGR 6.3% is retained-earnings accumulation on flat revenue (-2% 5yr) and falling EPS (-6.8% 5yr); a 3% mid-cycle revenue growth splits the difference and matches the base path's years 4-6
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+6.3%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (-2.0%) and EPS (-6.8%) CAGRs: book value compounds through retained profit while revenue and per-share earnings have shrunk since the FY2021 peak (EPS 0.244 -> 0.147). Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computable: the series is negative at both 3-year and 5-year endpoints (owner FCF FY2020 806.9, FY2022 -279.7, FY2025 -58.4) and averaged only ~RMB90m/yr over FY2018-25.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income, applied across the history: FY2018 471.2, FY2019 -161.0, FY2020 806.9, FY2021 42.2, FY2022 -279.7, FY2023 -285.7, FY2024 179.0, FY2025 -58.4 (RMB m). SBC was 0.6/0.3/0 thereafter, so the SBC adjustment is immaterial; the gap between profit and cash is working capital, not compensation.

base.cash_tax_rate_note: combined driver: cash tax 8% ramping to 13% plus ~7pp NCI leakage on EBIT (see inputs.nci_treatment)

bull.cash_tax_rate_note: same cash-tax ramp as base plus ~1pp more NCI leakage: the bull growth is titanium/aerospace, 32.4% of which belongs to TG Tech minorities

bear.cash_tax_rate_note: lower NCI leakage (titanium stays depressed, so less profit accrues to TG Tech minorities) on the same cash-tax ramp

scenario_narratives.base: FY2025 was the 'bottoming-out and rebound' year management calls it: H1 FY2026 revenue +5.5% and gross margin 24.8% (from 18.9%) as domestic DS/HSS demand recovered, June alloy-cost pass-through stuck, and the consumer-electronics customer resumed titanium-frame products in Q4 2025. Revenue grows 5% in FY2026 then fades to 2.5% -- a modest premium to eight flat years -- and the EBITDA margin eases from 20.5% to a 19.8% mid-cycle level equal to the FY2020-25 average. Capex runs at 7% of revenue, below D&A, because the asset base was built out in FY2021-22; working capital absorbs 45 cents of every incremental revenue dollar but stops growing faster than sales. The redeemable capital in TG Tools keeps being refinanced with bank debt rather than paid from cash. Terminal value is capped at 12x year-10 FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Powder metallurgy and plasma-atomised titanium powder become real revenue lines, aerospace-grade titanium wire (AMS4931) and nuclear-fusion steels scale from first orders, and the Thailand tools plant neutralises US tariffs on cutting-tool exports. Revenue compounds 8% for two years and 5-7% through year 5; mix shift to high-end grades lifts the EBITDA margin to 23%, above any year in the FY2018-25 history. The cost is heavier capex (7.5% of revenue) and more profit leaking to TG Tech's 32.4% minorities, which is why the combined tax/leakage driver runs ~1pp above base. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2025 titanium shock recurs -- another handset generation drops titanium, or a second large customer does -- while US tariff escalation and a weak Europe push HSS and cutting-tool exports down again; revenue falls 4% in FY2027 and the EBITDA margin drops to 15.5-16%, roughly the FY2019 level, before recovering only to 17%. Receivable terms to European customers keep lengthening and loss allowances (already 5.1% of receivables) rise, so working capital absorbs 50% of any revenue growth. With RMB4.4bn of debt-like liabilities against RMB1.9bn of cash and deposits, the dividend becomes the balancing item. Terminal growth 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default: a single consumer-electronics customer's design decision moved the titanium segment -17% and group gross margin ~7pp in one year, export segments carry live US-tariff risk, and eight years of ~2%-of-revenue owner-FCF conversion with rising debt is a pattern the base case assumes breaks. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- titanium recovery, aerospace/nuclear commercialisation on undisclosed timelines, and tariff relief -- and management guidance is qualitative with no numeric targets. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated specialty-steel, tools and titanium business on mid-cycle owner FCF built from components, charging working capital on growth, NCI as profit leakage, and the TG Tools redeemable capital as debt. The market capitalisation (~HK$7.8bn, ~RMB6.7bn) implies ~17x FY2025 attributable earnings and ~9.5x EV/EBITDA, a multiple that appears to carry a sum-of-the-parts premium for the BSE-listed TG Tech stake rather than the cash the group has actually produced. This model does not give credit for that re-rating: TG Tech's flows are valued inside the consolidated DCF at the same 9% rate and 12x cap as the steel business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital normalisation: the modelled 8-9% owner-FCF margin versus a realised ~2% over FY2018-25 is the dominant assumption; if receivables and inventories keep growing on flat revenue, every scenario here is too high.
Customer concentration in titanium alloy wire (consumer electronics) -- demonstrated in FY2025.
US/EU tariff policy on HSS, die steel and cutting-tool exports (27-57% of segment revenue).
NCI leakage treated as a constant ~7-8pp of EBIT; if TG Tech raises further equity at the subsidiary the parent's economic share falls below 67.6%.
CNY-built 9% WACC: a mechanical CAPM gives ~6.5%; the premium is a judgment on governance, liquidity and size, and the sensitivity grid shows its cost.
FX bridge CNY->HKD at 1.1721 is dated 2026-10-10 and is not refreshed by refresh_price.py.
Terminal value capped at 12x; the Gordon value at 9%/2.5% is ~16x, so the cap binds and the valuation is deliberately below a growth-perpetuity reading.
